trust_decision.summary: Whether a requested OAuth redirect_uri belongs to a client's registered redirect URIs is decided in DefaultRedirectResolver.redirectMatches/hostMatches; with matchSubdomains defaulting to true, the host check is a suffix match (requested.endsWith(registered)), so any host ending in the registered host string passes.

landing_point.why: The advisory title names DefaultRedirectResolver, and hostMatches is the only host-comparison method in it.

fix_sites.module_kind: core protocol library (redirect resolver used by HTTP handler)

fix_sites.entry_point: same authorize routes; field default matchSubdomains=true and redirectGrantTypes incl. 'implicit' consulted in resolveRedirect (DefaultRedirectResolver.java:65-72)
fix_sites.module_kind: default configuration (field defaults/setter) in the same class

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Both fix hunks are in one class (fix.diff:5-37); no second implementation, wrapper or save/reload path was changed.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The token-endpoint redirect_uri check is a separate grant step (code redemption), not the authorize redirect named in the advisory. A solver could also argue that its plain prefix match is legacy 'add by Crystal.Sea' code that is only defence in depth once the authorize redirect is exact.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Registered redirect URIs match by path prefix on the same scheme and host (registered https://app/cb accepts https://app/cb/sub?x=1). An exact-string fix such as ExactMatchRedirectResolver breaks clients that rely on this. A client with several comma-separated registered URIs must still match any one of them, and a single registered URI is used when redirect_uri is omitted.

O6_input_shapes: requested host that ends with the registered host string, with no dot boundary (e.g. attacker-registered-host suffix) - closed by equals
true subdomain of the registered host - closed by equals

O7_producer.where: maxkey-entity/src/main/java/org/dromara/maxkey/entity/apps/oauth2/provider/client/BaseClientDetails.java:169-171 (registered URIs split from one comma-delimited DB string, without trimming)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Token endpoint code redemption checks the redirect_uri with a raw string startsWith against registered URIs. That is a prefix match with no host boundary, and the code is not bound to the stored authorize redirect (the exact-match check is commented out).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a different endpoint (/authz/oauth/v20/token, /oauth2/token) and a different grant step. The advisory is about where the code is sent, not about redeeming it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file and package (provider.code vs provider.endpoint), same module

O8_uncovered_routes.route: When a client has no registered redirect URIs, resolveRedirect returns any requested redirect_uri unchecked.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Inherited Spring Security OAuth behaviour for unconfigured clients. A solver could call it a configuration matter.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: redirectMatches compares scheme and host but never the port, so the same host on any port passes. It also canonicalises after a URLDecoder.decode in the endpoint (decode-then-check differential).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Same host stays within the client's own origin set. Ports are a deployment detail.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as landing point; decode at AuthorizationEndpoint.java:174

O8b_injection_room.sibling: CAS service validation that uses a startsWith/endsWith host match instead of Strings.CS.equals
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: CAS deployments commonly want service-URL patterns, so a maintainer could plausibly loosen this to prefix/host matching. The Cas10 and Cas30 copies (Cas10AuthorizeEndpoint.java:109, Cas30AuthorizeEndpoint.java:87) are the same check in different files.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: approval POST re-resolving a redirect from approvalParameters with a lenient matcher
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The approval handler already takes request parameters (line 249). Re-reading redirect_uri there would be a natural maxkey-style addition.

O9_family: OAuth redirect_uri allow-list matching (CWE-183 permissive list / host suffix match)

O10_build.toolchain: Gradle (gradlew at repo root, multi-module), Spring Boot
O10_build.project_tests: None: maxkey-protocols/maxkey-protocol-oauth-2.0 has no src/test directory. DefaultRedirectResolver can be unit-tested without services; the full endpoint needs MySQL/Redis config (not verified).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change hostMatches to endsWith("." + registered) or set matchSubdomains=false, leaving the token-endpoint startsWith check and the port/no-registered-URI paths alone.

out_of_scope_notes: AuthorizationCodeTokenGranter.java:98 dereferences redirectUri without a null check (robustness, not this protection).

The authorize handler still serves response_type=token (AuthorizationEndpoint.java:199,268) after 'implicit' is removed from redirectGrantTypes; whether the implicit granter is still enabled was not checked.
CAS/SAML logout endpoints append redirect_uri into logout URLs (CasLogoutEndpoint.java:62, LogoutSamlEndpoint.java:77): a separate open-redirect surface.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell sizing done).
